article_title: Helping English Learners Rise to the Challenge of Complex Texts
citation: Helping English Learners Rise to the Challenge of Complex Texts. (2014). WestEd R&D Alert, Vol. 14, No. 3. http://ell.stanford.edu/teaching_resources/ela
title: QTEL approach: rigorous academic content and academic English taught simultaneously with expert support
description: The Quality Teaching for English Learners (QTEL) initiative holds that secondary ELL students can master rigorous academic content quickly and deeply rather than waiting years to learn English mechanics first. It works on the premise that students will rise to the challenge of rigorous subject matter if it sparks their interest, if they receive appropriate support, and if academic content and academic English language skills are taught simultaneously, as a single, integrated process. The article presents this as a counter to the traditional belief that ELL students need seven years of English before tackling complex academic content.
requirements: Teachers must make dramatic shifts in their beliefs and practices to master this instructional approach
target_learners: middle school and high school English language learners at intermediate English proficiency
target_learning_goals: academic English listening, speaking, reading, and writing
examples: The Persuasion across Time and Space unit was piloted in five urban school districts through a partnership between the Understanding Language initiative at Stanford and WestEd's Teacher Professional Development Program.

article_title: The Impact of Quantum Teaching Strategy on Student Academic Achievements and Self-Esteem in Inclusive Schools
citation: Gunarhadi, Mustapa Kassim & Abdull Sukor Shaari. (2014). THE IMPACT OF QUANTUM TEACHING STRATEGY ON STUDENT ACADEMIC ACHIEVEMENTS AND SELF-ESTEEM IN INCLUSIVE SCHOOLS. Malaysian Journal of Learning and Instruction: Vol. 11 (2014): 191-205. http://mjli.uum.edu.my/
title: Quantum Teaching content sequence: enroll, experience, demonstrate, and celebrate
description: The content element of Quantum Teaching follows a five-step lesson sequence proposed by DePorter (1992). The teacher first "enroll"s students to capture interest, curiosity, and attention; then has them "experience" content through exploration, which the article says better maintains long-term memory than reading or listening, followed by discussion, verification, and labeling of concepts; then students "demonstrate" their capability, followed by reflection and repetition to strengthen nerve connections; and finally the class "celebrate"s to appreciate those who finished tasks successfully, providing new energy for upcoming learning.
requirements: Exploration activities followed by discussion, verification, and labeling of discovered concepts
Reflection and repetition after demonstration to strengthen nerve connections
constraints: The article presents this sequence as part of the Quantum Teaching framework rather than as an independently tested component
target_learners: sixth-grade students in inclusive elementary schools
target_learning_goals: content mastery in Bahasa Indonesia and Science
student confidence through demonstration and celebration
examples: In the study, the content element was implemented through integrated themes: language skills through drama for Bahasa Indonesia and natural environment for Science

article_title: The Impact of Quantum Teaching Strategy on Student Academic Achievements and Self-Esteem in Inclusive Schools
citation: Gunarhadi, Mustapa Kassim & Abdull Sukor Shaari. (2014). THE IMPACT OF QUANTUM TEACHING STRATEGY ON STUDENT ACADEMIC ACHIEVEMENTS AND SELF-ESTEEM IN INCLUSIVE SCHOOLS. Malaysian Journal of Learning and Instruction: Vol. 11 (2014): 191-205. http://mjli.uum.edu.my/
title: Quantum Teaching context orchestration: atmosphere, foundation, environment, and lesson design
description: The context element of Quantum Teaching assigns the teacher to orchestrate four aspects of the classroom learning setting. First, orchestrating the learning atmosphere creates intimacy, warmth, humor, and accountability with positive emotional bonds between teachers and students. Second, orchestrating a strong foundation commits teachers to learning behaviors aligned with positive values and lifelong learning. Third, orchestrating the learning environment makes it safe, comfortable, and fun. Fourth, orchestrating the lesson plan prepares students for success through strategies bridging teaching materials and students' prior knowledge.
requirements: Teacher commitment to creating learning behaviors in accordance with positive values inherent in students
Managing the learning environment to make it safe, comfortable, and fun to learn
constraints: The article presents this as the framework's context element rather than as an independently tested component
target_learners: sixth-grade students in inclusive elementary schools, including children with special needs
target_learning_goals: academic success through bridging prior knowledge
examples: The article contrasts this with conventional teaching characterized by fixed seating arrangement, a textbook approach, and teacher-dominated learning environments
